title: Tuna and Vegetable Kimbap-Style Rice Rolls
summary: Korean-inspired rice rolls filled with seasoned tuna, crisp vegetables and sesame-scented sushi rice. They make a satisfying pescatarian snack or light lunchbox bite.

ingredients.name: cucumber, deseeded and cut into thin sticks

steps: Put the rinsed sushi rice and vegetable stock in a saucepan with a tight-fitting lid. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 12 minutes, then turn off the heat and let it steam for 10 minutes without lifting the lid.
Tip the rice into a wide bowl. Stir in the rice vinegar, sugar, 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tbsp sesame oil, then spread the rice out slightly so it cools until warm but still pliable.
Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise and black pepper until creamy and evenly combined.
Heat 0.5 tbsp vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the carrot matchsticks and a pinch of salt, then stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until just softened but still bright. Transfer to a plate.

Add the spinach to the same pan with a splash of vegetable stock if needed and cook for 1–2 minutes until wilted. Squeeze out excess liquid, then season with the remaining 0.5 tbsp sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining 0.5 tbsp vegetable oil and pour in the beaten eggs. Cook as a thin omelette for 1–2 minutes per side until set, then slice into long strips.
Lay a sheet of baking paper or a clean tea towel on the worktop. Spread a quarter of the warm rice into a rough rectangle about 20 x 18 cm, pressing it firmly so it holds together.
Arrange a line of tuna, carrot, cucumber, spinach and egg across the lower third of the rice. Use the paper or towel to roll it up tightly, pressing as you go to make a compact log.

Repeat with the remaining rice and fillings. Brush the rolls lightly with any remaining sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds, then slice each roll into bite-sized pieces with a sharp, lightly oiled knife.
